verdict.rationale: Fellow's documented REST Developer API exposes recordings with diarized, timestamped transcripts (via the `include` parameter), action-item listing with filters and pagination, and notes and meeting recaps, authenticated by user-generated API keys. Self-serve access is gated: the API needs a paid plan and workspace-admin enablement. Workspace-wide 'every meeting' retrieval is limited to Enterprise Super Admin keys, and AI summaries are not explicitly enumerated as an API field. missing for 10: explicit documentation of AI summary fields in API responses, ungated self-serve key access without admin enablement or paid plan, non-Enterprise access across every meeting, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, my scripts can pull transcripts, summaries, and action items from every meeting through a documented API with self-serve keys

citations.quote: The Developer API opens that data to you: transcripts, structured notes, and more, all available through standard REST calls.
A Recording represents a meeting recap in Fellow, and associated metadata. Each Recording is associated with a Note, and can contain information such as: Diarized and timestamped transcripts
List action items with optional filters and pagination.
Generate a new API key for your application, giving it a descriptive name.
The API is available on any Fellow workspace with a paid plan, and can be enabled or disabled for all users from Workspace Settings > Developer > API
